subject: tool:savedregs
value: TRIAGE of the accepted corpus against claim.law.T19_savedregs-default-read-reports-the-postprocessor-not-the-compiler-on-a-pinned-function.20260903.v1. TRIAGE KEY, stated: a record is AT RISK when it (a) cites savedregs, (b) is about a function that is webfrank-PINNED, and (c) does not mention --raw. Raw `real` is NOT the key and cannot be - a pinned function reads real 0 by construction (AGENTS.md residual-work discipline 3), which is the same defect one layer down. CENSUS over 2088 accepted record files at 1370dce50, with pins read from config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json's real schema {version, units: {unit: [{function: name, ...}]}} = 52 units / 154 pinned functions: 44 accepted records cite savedregs, and they split TIER 1 (own function pinned, no --raw) 3, TIER 1b (own function pinned, cites --raw, sound) 4, TIER 2 (cites savedregs about another pinned function, no --raw) 13, TIER 3 (no pinned function anywhere, out of scope) 18. THE THREE TIER-1 RECORDS COVER ONLY TWO FUNCTIONS, so both were re-derived. (A) game/game/player::PlayerProcessPowerups - VERDICT DOES NOT FLIP: both reads print `ASSIGNMENT MATCHES` over an identical 13-row table. But the default read is still the weaker one in two ways it does not announce: it prints `ROWS THIS TABLE CANNOT SEE: 15 differing instruction row(s)` where --raw prints 28, and --raw adds a line the default omits entirely - `LIFETIME PERMUTATION: 2 live range(s) - r22->r24, r24->r22. Same role, different callee-saved register: a declaration-list fact, not a schedule one.` The two TIER-1 records on this function (attempt.SA_playerprocesspowerups-pool-literal-and-propagation-drive.20260902.v1 and attempt.SA_playerprocesspowerups-volatile-half-is-a-bijective-scratch-permutation.20260903.v1) keep their assignment conclusion and lose their completeness: a permutation the postprocessed read erases is exactly the class the second one reasons about. (B) game/enemy/enemy::do_enemies - VERDICT FLIPS, a textbook member of the 84. Default: `ASSIGNMENT MATCHES`. --raw: `ROLE MISMATCH on 6 web(s)`, plus `LATER-WEB MISMATCH: 2 definition(s)`, plus `LIFETIME PERMUTATION: 9 live range(s) - f25->f26, f26->f25, f27->f31, f28->f29, f29->f28, f31->f27, r29->r30 x2, r30->r29`, plus `DEFINITION-COUNT DIFFERS on r28 (5 vs 3), r29 (6 vs 7), r30 (5 vs 6)`, plus `EMISSION ORDER DIFFERS`. HOW MUCH ACTUALLY RESTS ON IT IS LESS THAN THE TIER SUGGESTS, AND THE REAL DEFECT IS ELSEWHERE. attempt.SB_do-enemies-neighbour-statement-closes-entry-schedule-window.20260902.v1 cites savedregs for exactly one thing - `savedregs: frame 136 both, stmw base r28 both` - and that pair is MODE-INVARIANT (both reads print `frame: target 136 ours 136   stmw base: target r28 ours r28`), while its permutation analysis is sourced from regnorm and fndiff, so its conclusions stand. What does NOT stand is its EXPIRY CHECK: it names `python tools/gdl/savedregs.py game/enemy/enemy.c do_enemies` and fires 'if the two EMISSION ORDER lines ever agree while ROLE MISMATCH persists' - but on a PINNED function the default read prints NEITHER string, so the check can never fire in either direction. That is an UNFALSIFIABLE DENIAL reached by a second, different mechanism than the dead-scratch-path one, and it is invisible to a path-existence screen because the tool it names is shipped and runs fine.
